blocks.content: RBAC, Role-Based Access Control, is Kubernetes's permission system, built from four cooperating object types, deciding exactly who is allowed to do exactly what, across the cluster.

RBAC is built from Role and ClusterRole (defining what actions are permitted) and RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding (defining who actually gets those permissions), each covered in its own topic later in this module.

blocks.alt: What is permitted, bound to who actually gets it, the whole system in one picture

blocks.content: 2. The Concrete Mechanism Behind API Server Authorization
blocks.text: 2. The Concrete Mechanism Behind API Server Authorization

blocks.content: This is exactly the authorization step introduced in the API Server topic back in the Architecture module, RBAC is the actual system implementing that step, deciding whether a given request should be allowed to proceed.

blocks.alt: The real, concrete implementation of the authorization step covered earlier in this course

blocks.content: RBAC rules can apply to human users, groups of users, or Service Accounts (covered in the next topic), the identity representing a Pod or process, RBAC does not distinguish fundamentally between a human and an automated caller.

blocks.alt: Users, groups, and Service Accounts, all checked by the exact same system

blocks.content: This is a foundational principle worth internalizing: RBAC is deny-by-default, without an explicit grant permitting a specific action, it is simply not allowed, there is no implicit permission anywhere in the system.

blocks.alt: Nothing permitted unless explicitly granted, the safe, default posture

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: RBAC is built from four object types, Role/ClusterRole (what) and RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding (who), the actual mechanism behind API server authorization.
It checks users, groups, and Service Accounts uniformly, and operates on a deny-by-default basis, nothing is permitted without an explicit grant.
